requirement:
Build a simple privacy-friendly Python FastAPI URL shortener with SQLite and analytics. Include pytest tests under tests/. Clarify ambiguous product decisions before planning implementation. Use only the installed FastAPI, Pydantic, pytest, httpx and Python standard library; do not add dependency manifests.
Clarification: Use our established simple V1 scope: public statistics for anyone with the code, no authentication on the generated shortener API; no expiry or deletion; HTTP 302 redirects; only a single aggregate click count per link. Do not collect or store IP addresses, user agents, referrers, timestamps, country, daily/hourly analytics, or visitor identifiers. Count all successful redirects without bot classification. Create a new unique server-generated seven-character case-sensitive alphanumeric code for every submission, including duplicate URLs. Use secrets for code generation, SQLite uniqueness, and bounded collision retries. No custom aliases. Retain aggregate counts indefinitely. Accept HTTP/HTTPS URLs only, validate a hostname and maximum length 2048, never fetch submitted URLs server-side; private-address destinations are allowed for this local demo. Derive short_url from the request base URL. Use POST /links, GET /r/{code}, GET /links/{code}/stats. Use synchronous handlers for SQLite operations and typed input models, malformed input HTTP 422, missing code HTTP 404. Include a create_app factory with injectable database path, pytest tests and README startup instructions. No additional dependencies or manifests. These decisions resolve the questions; proceed to planning.

activity_completed: plan; attempts=1; Plan for a simple V1 privacy-friendly URL shortener, following the clarified decisions, which supersede the earlier acceptance criteria and defaults. The routes are POST /links, GET /r/{code} and GET /links/{code}/stats. Stats are public and need no auth. Redirects use 302. Each link stores only a single aggregate click count, so there is no per-click data, no IP, user agent, referrer, timestamp, country or visitor ID, and no bot classification. Every submission gets a new 7-character case-sensitive alphanumeric code from secrets. SQLite enforces uniqueness through a PRIMARY KEY, and collisions are retried a bounded number of times. There are no custom aliases, expiry or deletion. URLs must be http/https, have a hostname and be at most 2048 characters; they are never fetched, and private addresses are allowed. short_url is derived from the request base URL. The app is built by create_app(db_path) with synchronous handlers and Pydantic input models. Malformed input returns 422 and an unknown code returns 404. The layout is a top-level package `shortener` (main.py/app.py, db.py, models.py) plus tests/ and a README with startup instructions. No dependency manifests are added.
